weather.tip: 100% rain chance today — carry an umbrella, build in extra travel time, and expect waterlogging on the usual low-lying stretches during your commute.

around.headline: Four killed as SUV hits divider on Chennai-Bengaluru expressway
around.summary: Four people from Pune died after their SUV crashed into a divider on the Chennai-Bengaluru expressway, per The Siasat Daily and The Times of India. If you're driving this corridor, treat divider-crash reports as a reminder to slow down on unfamiliar high-speed stretches, especially at night.
around.source: The Siasat Daily, The Times of India

around.headline: Metro Pink Line clears Railway Board hurdle — October launch likely
around.summary: The Railway Board has cleared BEML trains to run on the Pink Line's elevated section, removing a key hurdle with an October opening now considered likely, per Deccan Herald and The Hindu. Worth watching if your commute could shift once the line opens — the launch date has slipped before.

around.headline: Bengaluru may get 'waste wardens' as citizen involvement pushed in garbage overhaul
around.summary: A proposed overhaul would bring in citizen "waste wardens" and ward-level planning to boost segregation and collection monitoring, per The Hindu and The Times of India. If your ward adopts this, expect closer checks on how you segregate wet and dry waste at the door.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: Karnataka calls it worst drought in 150 years, announces ₹2,500 farmer aid
around.summary: With 217 taluks reeling under a rain deficit, Karnataka announced ₹2,500 aid for farmers and is seeking a 'national disaster' tag for the drought, per The Times of India. A drought this widespread is also a signal to watch for tighter water-supply management in the city in the months ahead.

around.headline: Bengaluru tech funding hits $4.4bn this year — nearly matches next 5 cities combined
around.summary: Startup funding raised by Bengaluru-based companies this year has reached $4.4 billion, almost equal to the combined total of the next five Indian cities, per The Times of India. A sign the city's job market in tech and startups is staying relatively resilient even as some sectors slow elsewhere.

around.headline: UPI merchant charges: banks told not to let shops pass costs to customers
around.summary: The government has directed banks to ensure merchants don't pass on UPI transaction charges to customers, per The Times of India. If a shop tries to add a 'UPI fee' at checkout, you're within your rights to push back — or pay cash instead.

around.headline: EC's flawed SIR process still leaving valid voters off draft rolls
around.summary: A report on the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision found valid voters getting left off draft electoral rolls despite repeated verification attempts, per The Indian Express — an issue that earlier this month also hit several Bengaluru assembly seats with disproportionate deletions. If you haven't checked your name on the draft roll yet, do it before the correction window closes.

events.name: Neev Literature Festival — 10th edition
events.note: The city's annual literature festival returns for its tenth edition, per The Hindu.

events.name: Blue & Behold: Cyanotype Exhibition
events.note: A weekend exhibition of cyanotype (blue-toned) photographic art bringing together homegrown artists, per The New Indian Express.

events.name: Viva La Vino wine-tasting festival
events.note: Sommeliers host an approachable, unpretentious wine-tasting festival for the city, per The Hindu.

events.name: Hiriyara Jaatre — fair for elders
events.note: An annual fair dedicated to senior citizens returns to the city, per Deccan Herald.

street_smart.title: You're job-hunting and get a WhatsApp message: a 'recruiter' says you're selected for a work-from-home data-entry job paying ₹35,000/month, no interview needed. To 'lock in' the offer and receive your starter kit, you just need to pay a ₹2,000 registration fee — fully refundable after your first month. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen rotation (fake job offers & deposit fraud) — not used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks; no matching incident in today's feeds.
street_smart.situation: You've been applying to jobs for weeks with no response. This message arrived out of nowhere, addresses you by name, and the recruiter replies instantly and warmly on chat.

choices.text: Pay the ₹2,000 registration fee right away — it's refundable, and the pay is good for a work-from-home role.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Legitimate employers never charge candidates to get hired — recruitment costs are the company's expense, not yours. 'Refundable' fees are almost never returned; instead, paying once usually triggers further demands (a 'training kit' fee, a 'verification' fee), and the job itself typically doesn't exist.

choices.text: Independently look up the company on its official website or LinkedIn, call a number you find there (not one the recruiter gave you), and don't pay anything to receive a job offer.
choices.feedback: Correct. Verifying through a channel the recruiter doesn't control is the only way to confirm the offer is real. And the rule holds regardless of what you find: a genuine employer will never ask you to pay to start working for them.

choices.text: Ask the recruiter to first send an official offer letter and employee ID, then decide about the fee.
choices.feedback: Risky. Scammers can produce convincing offer letters and fake ID cards in minutes — a professional-looking document proves nothing. Only independently confirmed contact details (not anything sent to you in the chat) actually verify legitimacy.

choices.text: Just ignore the message without replying, blocking, or reporting it.
choices.feedback: Risky. Ignoring it protects you, but the same number keeps targeting other job-seekers. Blocking the contact and reporting it helps get it taken down before it scams someone else.

takeaways: A legitimate employer never asks a candidate to pay to get hired — any upfront 'registration', 'training kit', or 'security deposit' fee, refundable or not, is a red flag.
Verify a job offer through the company's official careers page or a number you found independently — never one given to you by the recruiter themselves.
Report suspicious recruitment messages to the National Cyber Crime helpline (1930) or cybercrime.gov.in so the number or account gets blocked before it reaches someone else.

quiz.question: Per today's report, Bengaluru's tech-startup funding this year is nearly equal to which of these?
options: The combined funding of the next 5 Indian cities
All of Mumbai's startup funding since 2010
Global venture capital funding for the decade
quiz.why: Bengaluru has held the top spot among Indian startup-funding hubs for well over a decade, thanks to its dense cluster of tech talent, VCs, and mature startup infrastructure.

quiz.question: How many taluks in Karnataka are reeling under a rain deficit in what's being called the worst drought in 150 years?
quiz.why: A taluk is an administrative sub-division of a district in Karnataka — the state has around 240 of them in total, so 217 affected is a large majority.

quiz.question: What cleared today, bringing Bengaluru Metro's Pink Line closer to an October opening?
options: Railway Board approval to run BEML trains on the elevated section
Full public inauguration of the line
quiz.why: The Pink Line has been one of Bengaluru Metro's most delay-prone corridors, so a Railway Board clearance for actual train operations is a more concrete milestone than another announced deadline.

quiz.question: What does "SIR", the ongoing electoral-roll exercise mentioned in today's report, stand for?
quiz.why: SIR is conducted by the Election Commission of India to verify and update electoral rolls booth by booth, and its draft lists can be checked and corrected by voters within a set window.

quiz.question: Which is the smallest Indian state by area?
quiz.why: Despite its small size, Goa has one of India's highest per-capita incomes, driven heavily by tourism.
